branch_pointer integration friction hit 2026-06-02 (orphan-branch leftover-claim caused a 5-step loop). THREE sub-drifts: (1) action=append did NOT auto-fill `session` from CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID — the MCP server process env lacked the var, so the appended pointer carried null session → pre-push branch-tree mirror keeper HARD-BLOCKED the dev push ('null/empty session'). Workaround: pass session= explicitly (got it via echo $CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID in a shell). Fix: funnel-self-satisfy — branch_pointer should resolve session from the shell/git config when the env var is absent, or fail LOUDLY at append time (not silently write a null that only blocks at push). (2) action=append/update with push_dev=True COMMITS the pointer onto the CURRENT branch (HEAD), not onto dev — when HEAD is a feature/leftover branch this advances the branch tip PAST the pointer's recorded `commit`, which then trips the 'shipped but branch ahead of recorded commit' mirror check, and the auto FF-push to dev fails repeatedly ('FF-push to dev failed after retry'). The pointer ledger commit belongs on dev regardless of current HEAD. Workaround that worked: finish the code merge, checkout dev, delete the branch, THEN append the shipped pointer from dev. (3) push_dev=False writes the ledger to the working tree but does NOT commit, leaving uncommitted churn the caller must reconcile (sibling of the auto_ledger_appends_strand_on_primary class). Net: registering a leftover/orphan branch in the live map at integration time is far harder than it should be. ROUND FIX: a dedicated 'integrate-from-dev' pointer path that always commits on dev FF-only + auto-resolves session, mirroring task_branch's salvage-ledger discipline.

INLINE-SELF-BRANCH ENV-WIRING DRIFT (2026-06-02): self-branched for a noc methodology/docs task with raw `git worktree add -b <branch> <path> origin/dev` instead of `noctus.dev.task_branch action=start`. Never bare `python cli.py` inside a raw `git worktree`. Codification target: noc-self-branch skill + KB self-branching-mode (add the 'raw-worktree-has-no-venv → use task_branch or main-venv+--worktree-path' note). Sibling of feedback_cross_product_tsc_cleanup_learnings (task_branch wire_env / dangling-symlink class).

8-WAY-SYNC EMBED-MOVES-WITH-DOC BLOCKS WORKTREE KB EDITS (2026-06-02): editing an EXISTING KB doc and committing fails `check_eight_way_sync` ("8-way sync FAILED, Commit aborted") because that doc's kb-embeddings are stale (cached.sha ≠ live). NEW KB files do NOT block (no prior cached sha). Inconsistency: the pre-commit AUTO-REFRESHES structural caches (agent-context, noc-graph via settle_structural_caches, zero-OpenAI) but does NOT auto-refresh EMBEDDING caches — yet the 8-way-sync gate BLOCKS on stale kb-embeddings for STAGED kb docs while only WARNING on unrelated code/corpus/memory embedding staleness. WORKAROUND used: `<main-repo>/venv/bin/python <worktree>/mcp/noctusai/cli.py --refresh-kb-embeddings --worktree-path <worktree>` (embeds worktree content → cache fresh vs worktree → commit passes). ROUND FIX options: (a) pre-commit auto-refreshes kb-embeddings for STAGED kb docs only (small, bounded OpenAI cost, like structural caches but embed) before the 8-way gate; OR (b) make the staged-kb-doc embedding check warn-only too (consistent two-tier-by-cost), deferring embed to push-time refresh. Hits any worktree KB-doc EDIT (recurring this session). Sibling of feedback_inline_self_branch_env_wiring (worktree tooling friction) + push-time-embedding-gate.

CORRECTION of the earlier 2026-06-02 entry "8-WAY-SYNC EMBED-MOVES-WITH-DOC BLOCKS WORKTREE KB EDITS" — that was a MISDIAGNOSIS. Empirically verified (2026-06-03): editing a KB file, staging it, and running the EXACT hook gate `--check-eight-way-sync --worktree-path <wt>` exits **0** — embedding-cache staleness (kb/code/corpus/memory) is severity=`warning` and the cli exit logic is `sys.exit(1 if any_high else 0)`, so embeddings NEVER block a commit (the pre-push hook batch-refreshes them — push-time-embedding-gate v4.1). The commit aborts I attributed to embeddings were actually the `[high]`-severity sub-keepers (check_agent_kb_alignment: a new PATTERNS/ doc unclaimed by any owns_kb/allowlist; check_claude_md_router word-cap) which my grep filters hid from view — and I then over-refreshed embeddings needlessly (wasted OpenAI cost + time). REAL lesson: (1) embedding staleness is warn-only — NEVER manually `--refresh-*` to "unblock" a commit; (2) when a commit aborts on 8-way-sync, the blocker is the `[high]` issue — grep/read for `[high]`, not the warning noise. ROUND FIX SHIPPED (same 2026-06-03 commit `0ddc331f`): cli.py `--check-eight-way-sync` now prints an explicit `✗ BLOCKED by N high-severity issue(s): <symbols>` line + a `(M advisory warning(s) — NOT blocking; embeddings refresh at push, don't manually refresh)` line, so the blocking-vs-advisory split is unmistakable and the misattribution cannot recur. Supersedes the earlier (wrong) entry; no further code change needed on the embed axis.

deploy-prod.yml's SSH step runs `ssh-keyscan -H "$VPS_HOST" >> known_hosts 2>/dev/null` under `bash -e`; on a TRANSIENT VPS-unreachable blip ssh-keyscan returns no key (or nonzero) and `set -e` aborts the whole step with exit 1 and NO message (observed 2026-06-30: a dry-run failed pre-`echo`, a re-run immediately succeeded). The deploy itself is fine — it's a flaky-edge false-negative. Root-fix candidates: (a) retry ssh-keyscan a few times with backoff before failing; (b) `ssh-keyscan ... || { echo '::warning::host-key scan failed (transient?) — retrying'; sleep N; ssh-keyscan ...; }`; (c) pre-seed a pinned known_hosts entry as a repo secret so the runner never depends on a live scan. Low severity (re-run clears it) but worth hardening — same transient-edge class the client-side _vps_ssh throttle addresses for our local tools. Sibling of feedback_vps_ssh_throttle_circuit_breaker.
